parts.problem_md:
Sophia invests \$500 at 6% simple interest per year for 3 years.

Work out the total interest earned.
parts.solution_md:
> *Simple interest means interest is earned only on the original amount*

> *Find 6% of \$500 by finding easier percentages first*

`table row cell 10 percent sign thin space of space $ 500 end cell equals cell $ 50 end cell row cell 5 percent sign space of space $ 500 end cell equals cell $ 25 end cell row cell 1 percent sign space of space $ 500 end cell equals cell $ 5 end cell end table`

**[M1]**

> *Use 5% + 1% to find 6%*

`6 percent sign thin space of space $ 500 equals $ 25 plus $ 5`

> *Write down the total interest earned*

`$ 30`

**[A1]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always check if the question is asking you to find the total interest earned, or the total value of the money at the end. In this case it is the interest earned.

> **[mark-scheme]**

> 
> **A1**: Correct final answer.

parts.problem_md:
\$12000 is invested at a rate of n% per year simple interest. 
At the end of 3 years the value of the investment is \$12900.

Find the value of $n$.

$n$ = .................................
parts.solution_md:

> * *

$12900-12000=900$

> * *

> *Because it is simple interest, you can divide by 3 to work out how much interest is earned per year.*

> * *

$900\div3=300$

**[1]**

** **

> *Express the amount of interest per year, \$300, as a fraction of the original amount invested, \$12000, and multiply by 100 to express as a percentage.*

> * *

$\frac{300}{12000}\times100=2.5$

* ***[1]**

**2.5%** **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Six years ago a farmer invested \$3750 at a rate of 4% per year compound interest.

i) Calculate the total value of his investment after the 6 years. Give your answer correct to the nearest dollar.

\$ ............................................... [3]

ii) The farmer wants to spend his investment on buying goats. Goats cost \$126 each.

Work out the maximum number of goats he can buy **and **the amount of money left over.

Number of goats .............................................. Amount of money left over \$ ............................................... [4]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Use the compound interest formula: *`A equals P cross times open parentheses 1 plus r over 100 close parentheses to the power of n`* where *$P$* is the current amount, *$r$* is the percentage interest, and *$n$* is the number of repetitions  *

$P=3750$

$r=4$

$n=6$

> *Substitute these values into the compound interest formula and evaluate*

> * *

`A equals 3750 cross times open parentheses 1 plus 4 over 100 close parentheses to the power of 6`

**[1]**

$=3750\times1.04^{6}$

$=4744.946319...$

**[1]**

** **

> *Round to the nearest dollar*

`bold $ bold 4745`** [1]**

** **

** **

ii) *Divide the investment by the number of goats to determine the maximum number of goats that can be bought*

> * *

$4745\div126$$=37.65873016...$

**[1]**

> *The maximum number of goats must be the nearest whole number below this value.*

> *  *

> $37.65873016...\rightarrow37$* *

> *  Multiply this number of goats by *`$ 126`* to work out the total cost *

$37\times126=4662$

> *Subtract this value from the total investment to find the amount of money left over*
* *

$4745-4662$

**[1]**

$=83$

*  *

**Final answer:** **37 goats**** [1]**

`bold $ bold 83`** [1]**

equations.alt: equals 3750 cross times 1.04 to the power of 6

parts.problem_md:
Sonia wants to invest \$5000 for 6 years.

Bank A pays compound interest at a rate of 3.5% per year. 
Bank B increases the \$5000 by 22% at the end of 6 years.

Which bank will give Sonia the most money at the end of 6 years and by how much? You must show all your working.

![qp18-0580-13-paper-1-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/001-qp18-0580-13-paper-1-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths.png)
parts.solution_md:
> *Bank A*

> *An increase of 3.5% means 103.5% of the original amount. Divide 103.5 by 100 to find the multiplier.*

> * *

$103.5\div100=1.035$

> * *

> *The multiplier will be applied 6 times, so multiply \$5000 by *$1.035^{6}$*.*

> * *

$5000\times1.035^{6}=6146.2766...$

**[1]**

> *Round to 2 decimal places (because it is money).*

> * *

`Bank space straight A space equals space $ 6146.28`

**[1]**

** **

> *Bank B*

> *An increase of 22% means 122% of the original amount. Divide 122% by 100 to find the multiplier.*

> * *

$122\div100=1.22$

> * *

> *Multiply \$5000 by the multiplier, 1.22.*

> * *

$5000\times1.22=6100$

* ***[1]**

`Bank space straight B space equals space $ 6100`

**[1]**

** **

> *Bank A will give Sonia the most money.*

> *Subtract the Bank B figure, \$6100, from the Bank A figure, \$6146.28 to work out how much more Bank A gives.*

> * *

$6146.28-6100=46.28$

> * *

**Bank ****A**** will give ****\$ 46.28**** more money**. **[1]**

equations.alt: 5000 cross times 1.035 to the power of 6 equals 6146.2766...

parts.problem_md:
Cody is aiming to save \$2000 in total.

They invest \$1750 in a savings account which pays 6.5% interest each year.

How many years will it take for the balance in the account to reach at least \$2000?
parts.solution_md:
*Find the amount in the account at the end of each year* *An increase of 6.5% will be a multiplier of 1.065*

*After 1 year there will be: 1750×1.065 = \$ 1863.75*

**[1]**

*This is not greater than 2000, so increase the amount by 6.5% again* *Round the answer to 2 decimal places*

*After 2 years there will be: 1863.75×1.065 = \$ 1984.89375 ≈ \$ 1984.89*

**[1]**

*This is still not greater than 2000, so increase the amount by 6.5% again* *Round the answer to 2 decimal places*

*After 3 years there will be: 1984.89×1.065 = \$ 2113.90785 ≈ \$ 2113.91*

> *This is now more than 2000*

**It will take ****3 years****  for the balance to reach more than \$2000 ****[1]**
